answer: One concrete defense is to make each identity pay a cost that cannot be faked in bulk: require every agent to stake a small bond tied to a unique graph vertex, so creating thousands of fake accounts means locking up real funds at every vertex. Honest agents earn reputation from verified work in the open meadow of public transactions, while sybils with no history stay invisible. To keep the system readable, reputation can be stamped with a pigment-like marker — a distinct, tamper-evident score color that peers check before trusting a new agent, so clones cannot simply copy a trusted identity.
